text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Infectious diseases (travel medicine) consultation in two weeks to establish the cause of the recurrent fevers, advise on antirelapse treatment, and plan pre-travel care for the deployment
  • Malaria testing between attacks: thick and thin blood smears, rapid antigen test, and Plasmodium species PCR sent to the reference laboratory; quantitative G6PD activity before any primaquine; blood count, kidney and liver tests
  • Fever action plan: a blood smear the same day for any fever, at home, at sea or after travel; carry a card stating his malaria history
  • Chloroquine for the blood stage (1,000 mg salt, then 500 mg at 6, 24 and 48 hours) and primaquine 30 mg base daily for 14 days for radical cure, with the normal G6PD result; blood count and bilirubin after the course; report dark urine, breathlessness or blue lips
  • Pre-travel plan for French Guiana and the Antilles: one dose of yellow fever vaccine with the certificate, hepatitis A, hepatitis B if not immune, typhoid; atovaquone-proguanil chemoprophylaxis for malaria areas; repellent, permethrin-treated clothing, screened or air-conditioned quarters and bed nets against mosquitoes, fleas, lice and mites; food and water precautions with standby azithromycin; primaquine terminal prophylaxis after leaving the malaria areas, and a malaria test for any fever after return

resource.title: Pierre Le Moyne d'Iberville synthetic care plan
resource.description: Primary care and travel medicine for a 43-year-old naval commander with recurrent fevers after service in malaria-endemic areas, who is preparing to lead a deployment to French Guiana and the French Antilles: recognizing relapsing Plasmodium vivax malaria after blood-stage treatment without antirelapse therapy, using PCR when smears are negative between attacks, testing G6PD quantitatively before primaquine, radical cure with chloroquine and primaquine, and relapse surveillance; then a full pre-travel consultation under the CDC Yellow Book 1705 and the IDSA travel medicine guideline: one dose of yellow fever vaccine and a valid certificate for French Guiana, hepatitis A, hepatitis B and typhoid vaccines, atovaquone-proguanil chemoprophylaxis, mosquito avoidance for dengue and chikungunya (no dengue vaccine for travelers), repellents for typhus, food and water precautions with standby treatment for travelers' diarrhea, terminal antirelapse therapy and fever evaluation after return; preventive care at 43; and a same-day visit for a skin abscess managed by drainage alone under the IDSA skin and soft tissue guideline.
